chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Ali ibn Rashid from the Master of the Camp (peace be upon him) said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, we are brought an item and it is said: 'This belonged to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)' while we are here, so what should we do?' He said, 'Whatever belonged to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) by reason of the Imamate belongs to me, and whatever is otherwise, it is inheritance according to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet.'

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (referring to Imam al-Baqir or Imam al-Sadiq depending on context, here likely al-Baqir as predecessor to al-Hadi's line of discussion or general reference)

ai.seo_question: How do Shia jurists distinguish between the personal property of the Imams and their property acquired due to their office of Imamate?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Hadi (peace be upon him) clarifies the dual nature of the Imams' possessions, distinguishing between assets acquired specifically due to their political and spiritual authority (Imamate) and those acquired as private individuals. The ruling establishes that while items tied to the office of Imamate are retained by the successor Imam, other assets are distributed as general inheritance according to the Quran and the Prophet's Sunnah, reflecting the practical application of inheritance law in Shia jurisprudence.
